_comment: The buildings and landmarks that are places in their own right.
WHY THIS EXISTS. Until now `locations` held sixteen outdoor regions and no
interiors at all, so there was nowhere to put an NPC who is indoors — which
is most of them, most of the day. A schedule saying 'Sleeping Dragon Inn' had
nothing to resolve to.
WHAT IS CURATED AND WHAT IS SOURCED. The list below is a judgement: which
buildings are worth being a location rather than a detail of one. Everything
about each building — the region it sits in, the quest that unlocks it, who
lives there — is read from its `{{Infobox location}}` by enrich/places.ts.
Nothing here is a fact typed in by hand.
TWO OF THESE ARE NOT WHERE YOU WOULD GUESS. The Museum is in The Narrows and
the Carpenter is on The Eastern Road, not in town. Both were read from the
page, and both are the reason this is sourced rather than assumed.
ROOMS ARE NOT LOCATIONS. Adeline's Office, the Manor's Dining Room and the
Inn's balcony are rooms inside a building, and there are hundreds of them.
They become the `activity_key` on a schedule block, which is what they are:
a named anchor inside a place, not a place you can be directed to.
REGIONS ALREADY IN vocab/locations.json ARE NOT REPEATED HERE, even where
they have an infobox — Sweetwater Farm's says `location=Mistria`, which means
the valley rather than the town, and importing it would file Hayden's farm
inside the town square.
ALIASES are the spellings seen in the wild, mostly in NPC schedule tables,
which are written by hand and inconsistently: 'Bath House' and 'Bathhouse',
'Manor' and 'Manor House', 'Inn' and 'Sleeping Dragon Inn'.
_quest_alias_comment: How a place page spells a quest, when it does not spell it the way the
The Summit's infobox gates it on 'Beautification of Mistria'. No such quest
exists: the page for it 404s, and the quest the Narrows names for the same
town-improvement work is 'Beautification Project', which redirects to the
Quests page and is in our dataset. So the Summit's gate was pointing at
nothing — `checkGates` caught it, which is the entire reason that check was
One entry only. This is a spelling table, not a place to make two different
quests into one because it would be convenient.
_regions_comment: Regions that already exist in vocab/locations.json, listed here only so
their `unlock=` is read. Two of the nine are behind a story quest — the
Deep Woods needs the Fire Seal broken and the Summit needs Mistria
beautified — and until now nothing in the dataset knew that.
It matters more than it looks. Everything found in the Deep Woods is
unreachable on day one, and a companion app that lists Glowing Mushroom
under 'findable now' without saying so is sending a new player somewhere
they cannot go. The gate turns that into a result tagged `locked`, which is
shown rather than hidden — a player wants to know it exists.
No `id` or `kind` here: the record already exists and only gains a field.
